lesson.title: ver ↔ for- Cognate Set
lesson.subtitle: Twelve ver- words mapped to English for- words — the payoff arc

hook.title: The Payoff Arc
hook.content: You have been collecting ver- previews since topic 2: vergessen teased the arch from lesson one's neighborhood, verboten hid in plain sight, verkaufen waited in the modal lessons. Now the arc completes: ver- is English for-, systematically. vergessen/forget, verlieren/forlorn-lose, verboten/forbidden, verfahren? — the drive-astray verb (sich verfahren — get lost driving!). Twelve words, one prefix, one Germanic story: the for- that English kept in forget, forgive, forbid, forlorn, forgo, forsake — German kept as ver- and used on everything.

footnotes.title: The Full for- Ledger
footnotes.content: English for- words: forget, forgive, forbid, forlorn, forgo, forsake, forswear, forbeat? — the survivors are few because English lost the PREFIX as a living tool. German ver- is still productive: veralten (grow old), sich verfahren (drive astray), sich verschreiben (mis-prescribe). One dead prefix, one living one. (grow old), sich verfahren (drive astray), sich verschreiben (mis-prescribe). One dead prefix, one living one.

pattern.title: The Twelve, Mapped
pattern.content: vergessen ↔ forget (get + for). verlieren ↔ lose (forlorn = for-lost). verboten ↔ forbidden. verstehen ↔ understand (for-stand? no — but stehen/stand rhyme!). verkaufen ↔ sell (the cheap-loan with ver-). versuchen ↔ to try (the seek-out verb — suchen inside!). sich verfahren ↔ get lost driving (fahren inside!). verzeihen ↔ forgive? hint — zeihen (accuse) — ver-zeihen is 'un-accuse', forgive's true twin. vermeiden ↔ avoid (meiden = meet? no — 'shun'; mid in English 'methinks' family? hint only). verbinden ↔ bind (connect — verbinden/binden!). verbringen ↔ spend time (bringen inside!). The system: ver- + a root you own = an English for- word or a meaning-shifter.
pattern.linguist_note: ver- does three jobs: loss (verlieren), error (sich verfahren), and transformation (verkaufen — sell IS a transformation of goods). English for- kept the loss/error jobs (forget, forsake) and lost the rest. The prefix jobs are the drift story.

exercises.prompt: The ledger — match each ver- verb with its English for-twin. Then recall earlier vocabulary in the short phrases:
exercises.target_answer: vergessen, verboten, versuchen, verlieren, verdienen, Wir können das bekommen, Wir können das verkaufen
exercises.meaning: forget; forbidden; to try (seek-out); forlorn / lost; to earn / deserve; We can receive that; We can sell that
exercises.explanation: One prefix, one story: ver- is for-, and the jobs split between loss, error, and transformation — verdienen is the transformation job (earn/deserve), where English's for- never survived to make 'for-earn'.

options: I got lost driving — the error-job of ver-
exercises.target_answer: I got lost driving — the error-job of ver-
exercises.explanation: ver- + fahren: the driving went WRONG. The error-job — same family as English 'for-' in forgo. Abfahren and einkaufen are fahren and kaufen's separable cousins: their prefixes fly, ver- never moves.
ver- + binden = bind together = connect. The noun die Verbindung (connection) keeps the root visible — and the feeling-nouns keep theirs: die Angst, die Hoffnung, nouns German and English share.

exercises.prompt: What English past-participle adjective is the twin of 'verboten'?
exercises.explanation: verbieten, verbot, verboten ↔ forbid, forbad(e), forbidden — the whole paradigm, twin for twin. Traurig runs no ver- at all: traurig ↔ dreary, the d → t shift doing the work alone.

exercises.prompt: Assemble: 'I try to understand German' (versuchen + zu + verstehen)
exercises.explanation: Two ver- verbs in one zu-ladder: versuchen (try) opens, zu verstehen (to understand — for-stand!) closes.

summary.outcome: Map twelve ver- verbs to their English for- twins and decode new ver- words by root.
summary.takeaway: ver- = for- (vergessen/forget, verboten/forbidden) — and its three jobs (loss, error, transformation) decode every new ver- word.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Next: be- & er- — the verb factory: bekommen, erinnern, erklären, and stress as the separable/inseparable test.

twist.prompt: Without looking back — rebuild the core sentence from ver ↔ for- Cognate Set (I try to understand German):
twist.explanation: Re-assembling "Ich versuche Deutsch zu verstehen" from scratch locks in the structural pattern of ver ↔ for- Cognate Set without relying on short-term echo.

verlieren.etymology_derivation: ver- (for-) + lieren from Proto-Germanic *leusaną — the same root as English lose; forlorn is 'utterly lost' (forleosan), the exact ver- construction. [wiktionary]

verstehen.etymology_derivation: Inseparable: ver- (for-) + stehen (stand). Past participle: verstanden (no ge-).

versuchen.context_translation: I am trying to find it.

verboten.etymology_derivation: ver- (for-) + bieten/bot — 'for-bidden' via the bid-root: bieten ↔ bid is the twin pair. [wiktionary]

verdienen.context_translation: She earns a lot of money.
verdienen.etymology_derivation: From ver- + dienen (to serve), a calque of Latin deservio - the same Latin verb that gave English deserve (via Old French deservir). [wiktionary][etymonline]

weiß.etymology_derivation: t → ß. Also first-person of wissen (ich weiß = I know/am wise).

traurig.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *dreuzagaz — English dreary is the cognate, with English d ↔ German t. [wiktionary]

angst.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *angustiz; the page names no English cognate (anguish/angry not cited) — treat as memorize. [wiktionary]

hoffnung.etymology_derivation: hoffen (to hope) + -ung: German hardened English p into pf-f, so hope became hoffen; the page lists English hoping as the cognate. [wiktionary]

einkaufen.etymology_derivation: ein (in) + kaufen (to buy) — buy in, do the shopping; the kaufen root is the German twin of English cheap. [wiktionary]

abfahren.etymology_derivation: ab (off) + fahren (to drive): to drive off — the same verb root as English fare. [wiktionary]

falls.context_phrase: Falls es regnet, bleibe ich hier.
falls.context_translation: In case it rains, I stay here.
falls.etymology_derivation: Presumably the genitive of Fall (case, fall — exact twin of English fall); in the case of a fall, that is in case. [wiktionary]

quittung.context_phrase: Können Sie mir eine Quittung geben?
quittung.context_translation: Can you give me a receipt?
quittung.etymology_derivation: From Middle High German quiten, to clear or release — the same French loan-family as English quit: a receipt quits your debt. [wiktionary]

mal.context_phrase: Komm ein Mal mit ins Kino.
mal.context_translation: Come along to the cinema one time.
mal.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *mēlą — English meal is the documented cognate (Mahl is the same word); ein Mal counts the times, as in piecemeal. [wiktionary]
